name: gate4-alltoall-cross-node
description: All-to-all spanning more than one node, i.e. EP=16 and EP=32. This is the configuration reported as failing with PTLTE_NOT_FOUND once the expert all-to-all crosses nodes, and at 32 ranks with an NCCL 'unhandled system error' during initialisation. It is also the case the shipped container test suite has no equivalent of.

gates.name: alltoall_passed
gates.note: The headline gate. A failure here is the reported defect reproducing.

gates.name: payload_correct
gates.note: Correctness across the fabric, not just completion without error.

gates.name: uneven_splits_correct
gates.note: Uneven cross-node dispatch is what a real MoE expert exchange looks like.

gates.name: communicator_churn_clean
gates.note: Repeated cross-node communicator creation. Portals table entries and other CXI resources are finite; exhaustion appears on the Nth creation, not the first.

gates.name: actually_crossed_nodes
gates.note: Guards the test itself. Without this a misconfigured job could satisfy every gate above while never leaving the node -- which is precisely how the reported regression survived validation.

gates.name: bandwidth_large_message_gbps
gates.note: PROVISIONAL -- recalibrate from a measured baseline. A LUMI-G node has 4x200 Gbit/s Slingshot NICs shared by 8 ranks, so per-rank cross-node bandwidth is a fraction of the 23.75 GB/s the container's own suite asserts for a single process per node.
